citation: Wiggins, M., Sawtell, M., & Jerrim, J. (2017). Learner Response System: Evaluation report and executive summary. London: Education Endowment Foundation.
report_number: EEF project: Learner Response System (UCL Institute of Education evaluation, November 2017); EEF Digital Technology funding round, in collaboration with Nominet Trust; intervention developed by Edge Hill University. ERIC: not located under a separate ED number; PDF from EEF.
design: Cluster RCT; assignment = SCHOOL level (stratified by 2013 performance into 10 strata); 97 schools randomised (49 intervention / 48 control); ~6,572 pupils. Intervention = teacher professional development to deliver the Learner Response System (handheld classroom-feedback devices): 2-day baseline training + half-termly training over the year (7 training days yr1, 2 days yr2). Primary outcomes = Year 6 KS2 SATs maths and reading (national standardized tests). Single intervention arm vs business-as-usual control. Two analysis cohorts: Cohort A = pupils who received ONE year of intervention (KS2 sat May 2015); Cohort B = pupils who received TWO years (KS2 sat May 2016). Effectiveness trial, England (NW + W Yorkshire LAs), high-FSM primary schools.
problems: Registry row 132 codes the assignment level as 'Teacher/Class', but the report is explicit that randomisation was at the SCHOOL level (a stratified cluster RCT with school as the unit of allocation; class-level randomisation was considered but rejected to avoid within-school contamination). Coarse registry coding aside, design recorded here matches the actual report. The report reports effect sizes as COHEN'S d (impact coefficient / pooled SD; see p.17 and p.30), not Hedges' g; J small-sample correction applied here is ~0.9997 (df>2,800) so g equals d to >=4 dp. Impact SE not printed directly; g_se derived from the reported 95% CI on the effect-size scale (SE = CI width / (2 x 1.95996)). These CIs already incorporate Huber-White standard errors clustered at the school level, so the estimates are cluster-adjusted (cluster_adjusted=true). ICC recorded per outcome is the OBSERVED analysis-stage ICC from the power tables (Tables 5-6, 'Primary analysis' rows), not the design-stage 0.15. n_clusters recorded is schools in the primary analysis (94 for cohort A maths/reading; 93 for cohort B). Cohort A showed baseline KS1 imbalance favouring control (~0.14 SD); the OLS model adjusts for KS1 pretest + stratum dummies. KS2 maths/reading raw means and SDs differ in scale across cohorts (cohort A used raw NPD marks ks2_mattotmrk/ks2_readmrk; cohort B used scaled scores ks2matscore/ks2readscore) because of the 2016 KS2 assessment change. Two cohorts are DISTINCT pupil samples receiving different doses (1 vs 2 years), not two follow-up waves of the same pupils; both are headline primary outcomes and are extracted (4 full-sample contrasts). FSM/boys/girls subgroups (Tables 12-15) and maths-subdomain secondary outcomes (Tables 16-17) were NOT extracted as separate records (subgroups are non-randomised subsets; subdomains are subscales). This is distinct from Wiggins et al. 2019 (a separate EEF SCHOOL-level secondary (Years 7-12) RCT, (P)CK goal, two arms, registry row 133).

effect_sizes.arm_label: Learner Response System (single TPD arm) vs business-as-usual control -- Cohort A (one year of intervention)
effect_sizes.test_name: KS2 maths SATs (NPD ks2_mattotmrk, total raw mark)
effect_sizes.timepoint: post (May 2015 KS2, end of 1 year of intervention)
effect_sizes.g_method: Report's Cohen's d = OLS impact coefficient (KS1 pretest + stratum-adjusted) / pooled SD; multiplied by Hedges J = 1-3/(4*df-1) with df=n_model-2=2835 (J=0.99974), so g=0.00. g_se = (CI_hi-CI_lo)/(2*1.95996) from reported 95% CI (-0.13, 0.14); CIs use Huber-White SE clustered at school level; g_var = g_se^2.
